correctness.rationale: For each k>=2 the exact marker criterion is proved both ways. All adjacent-one targets force at least two distinct host ones in each d-level window, giving R*d>=2(k-1) and the rigorous lower bound. The mod-d two-residue construction has two markers in every d-window; first and last levels satisfy all three target gaps, including the b=0 distinct-marker boundary. The exact residue count gives R<=ceil(2(k-1)/d)+2. The integer balanced-product identity optimizes d and produces the all-k envelope. The elementary squeeze proves the sharp limit. Exact BFS k=2..12, all small-host criterion comparison and construction checks k<=100 plus 150/200/300/500 passed from verifier.py; these finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The complete weight-two slice is a natural constant-composition restriction of classical subsequence universality and a structured shortest-common-supersequence language, relevant to indexing with sparse markers. The sharp nontrivial 2sqrt(2) leading overhead distinguishes this cover task from the full-language 2k threshold and the one-marker sqrt(k) law. A universal additive-two envelope and an explicit all-length covering construction are useful even though the remaining two-unit finite-length gap is open. The result is neither a table nor a simple parameter substitution.
